subject.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — UI dashboard and CLI command

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this first-class core AI-safety taxonomy and operator surface, and if so must it extend the existing diagnostics-stability subsystem rather than create a parallel store and API?
rationale: The answer establishes new core telemetry, plugin SDK, persistence, privacy, gateway protocol, CLI, and UI contracts; automation cannot safely choose those permanent owner boundaries.

options.title: Use the canonical diagnostics path
options.body: Approve the product direction only after the series is narrowed onto diagnostic stability, shared SQLite retention, bounded sanitization, classified RPCs, and direct UI/CLI proof.

options.title: Approve a separate safety subsystem
options.body: Explicitly accept a second diagnostics owner only with a reviewed persistence, retention, redaction, protocol-versioning, and migration contract.

options.title: Pause the series
options.body: Keep the tracking issue for design discussion and close or replace the implementation PRs until the core taxonomy and ownership direction is sponsored.

recommendation.title: Use the canonical diagnostics path
recommendation.body: Approve the product direction only after the series is narrowed onto diagnostic stability, shared SQLite retention, bounded sanitization, classified RPCs, and direct UI/CLI proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans gateway architecture, core runtime ownership, and a new public operator surface rather than a narrow UI repair.
